day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 4:00 PM. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome, GA via Condor flight at 16:00. Check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome on Chateau Drive. Freshen up, unpack, and get oriented. Take a short walk around the immediate hotel neighborhood to stretch your legs after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Rome's Historic Downtown for a relaxed first-evening stroll. Explore Broad Street, admire the Clocktower, and get a feel for the city layout. Browse any open local shops and enjoy the warm June evening (around 29°C). Keep it light since you just arrived.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit / airport food
meals.dinner: Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A near Chateau Drive for a quick, affordable first-night meal (~$8-12). Alternatively, grab groceries at a nearby Walmart or Kroger to stock up on breakfast items for the week.

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1 is rest and settling in. Pick up a city map or download the Rome, GA visitor app. Buy a reusable water bottle — June heat averages 29.8°C and hydration is essential. Budget tip: stock your room with snacks and breakfast items from a grocery store to save money throughout the week.

day_by_day.morning: Rome, GA Historic Downtown Art Walk — Start early (9:00 AM) before the heat peaks. Explore the vibrant murals, local galleries, and public art installations scattered throughout Downtown Rome. Begin at Broad Street and work your way through the arts district. Many murals and public installations are free to view. Pick up a self-guided art walk map from the Rome Area Council for the Arts if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Downtown Art Walk into the afternoon, visiting any open local galleries (many are free or low-cost entry). Stop by the Rome Area History Museum (~$5 entry) for cultural context. Rest in one of the shaded downtown parks during the hottest part of the day (2:00–3:30 PM). Explore the shops along Broad Street.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the cooler evening air back in Downtown Rome. Walk along the Oostanaula or Etowah River banks near the confluence (The Confluence area is a scenic free attraction). Watch the sunset over the rivers.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast with groceries purchased the night before (yogurt, fruit, granola bars) — ~$2-3
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Café or a local deli in Downtown Rome — budget sandwich or salad ~$10-13
meals.dinner: El Sombrero or another local Mexican restaurant in Rome for affordable, filling tacos or burritos ~$10-14

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and sunscreen. Carry water at all times. The art walk is entirely self-paced and mostly free — perfect for budget travelers. Check the Rome Area Council for the Arts website for any free gallery opening events happening this week.

day_by_day.morning: Chieftains Museum & Major Ridge Home Tour — Head out by 9:30 AM to this National Historic Landmark just minutes from Chateau Drive. Explore the fascinating Cherokee history and the beautifully preserved Major Ridge Home. Admission is typically low-cost (~$5-8 per person). Spend 2–3 hours absorbing the rich Native American and early American history.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, visit the nearby Myrtle Hill Cemetery, a free historic site with panoramic views of Rome and the rivers below — a hidden gem. Then return to the hotel for a midday rest during peak heat hours (2:00–4:00 PM). Alternatively, visit the Rome-Floyd County Library for free air-conditioned relaxation and local travel resources.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lock & Dam Park along the Coosa River for a free, scenic evening walk. The park offers beautiful river views and is a great spot for photography. Enjoy the cooler evening temperatures.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — ~$2-3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from grocery store items (sandwiches, fruit, chips) and eat at the Chieftains Museum grounds or a nearby park — ~$5-7
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli or a local pizza spot in Rome for an affordable dinner ~$10-13

day_by_day.notes: The Chieftains Museum is a must-see and very close to your hotel — one of the most historically significant sites in Northwest Georgia. Call ahead to confirm opening hours and tour times. Myrtle Hill Cemetery is free and offers some of the best views in Rome — don't skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Berry College Campus Art & Nature Walk — Drive or rideshare to Berry College (very close to Rome). Start early at 8:30–9:00 AM to enjoy the cooler morning temperatures. Explore the stunning Gothic architecture of the Ford Buildings, the on-campus art collections, and the scenic natural landscapes. Berry College has one of the largest college campuses in the world — the grounds are breathtaking and free to walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Berry College's nature trails and the historic mill area. The campus deer are a beloved attraction and often visible in the afternoon. Visit the Berry College Art Gallery if open (free). Return to the hotel by 3:00 PM for a rest during peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday evening in Downtown Rome — check local event listings for any free outdoor concerts, farmers markets, or community events (Rome often hosts weekend events in summer). Walk Broad Street and enjoy the lively Saturday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — ~$2-3
meals.lunch: Berry College area — bring a packed lunch or find an affordable café near campus ~$8-10
meals.dinner: Saturday treat: Harvest Moon Café or Broad Street Brewing Company (food menu) in Downtown Rome for a slightly elevated but still budget-friendly dinner ~$14-18

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is free to visit and absolutely stunning — the Gothic architecture rivals anything in Europe. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the campus is vast. Check Berry College's website for any public art events or exhibitions happening on campus during your visit. Saturday may have a local farmers market in Downtown Rome — great for cheap, fresh local food.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit your favorite Downtown Rome spots at a leisurely Sunday morning pace. Visit the Rome Farmers Market if running (typically Sunday mornings in season) for fresh local produce, artisan goods, and affordable snacks. Browse local art vendors and crafts — great for budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Coosa Valley Art Museum or any local gallery you may have missed earlier in the week. Many smaller galleries in Rome are free or donation-based. Spend time in air-conditioned comfort during the hottest afternoon hours. Alternatively, visit the Rome Tennis Center area and surrounding parklands for a free outdoor experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk at the Oostanaula River Greenway Trail — a free, scenic riverside trail perfect for an evening stroll. Enjoy the golden hour light over the water. This is a great photography opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Farmers Market breakfast — fresh pastry or local food stall item ~$4-6
meals.lunch: In-room or picnic lunch from farmers market purchases ~$5-8
meals.dinner: Taqueria El Nopal or another affordable local spot for a budget Sunday dinner ~$9-12

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to slow down and revisit highlights. Some attractions may have reduced Sunday hours — check ahead. The Greenway Trail is free and beautiful in the evening. Use this day to do laundry at the hotel if needed and plan your final days.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into Rome's street art scene — revisit the Historic Downtown Art Walk with fresh eyes and explore any murals or installations you may have missed on Day 2. Take your time photographing the artwork. Visit any local studios or artist workshops that may be open to the public (check local listings).
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip option: Drive to nearby Cave Spring, GA (~20 minutes from Rome) — a charming small town with a natural cave, a spring-fed swimming pool (very affordable entry ~$3-5), and historic architecture. Perfect for a hot June afternoon. The cave tour is budget-friendly and unique.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a final evening exploration. Walk the Historic Downtown one more time and pick up any last-minute souvenirs from local shops. Enjoy the warm June evening along the river.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — ~$2-3
meals.lunch: Cave Spring local diner or pack a lunch for the trip ~$7-10
meals.dinner: Broad Street area restaurant — try somewhere you haven't visited yet. Look for daily specials ~$11-15

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring is a wonderful hidden gem near Rome and very budget-friendly. The natural cave and swimming pool are refreshing on a hot June day. If you have a car, this is highly recommended. If not, focus on more Downtown Rome exploration and visit the Rome Area History Museum if you haven't yet.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — take a peaceful early walk along the Etowah River or the Greenway Trail one last time. Visit any remaining items on your Rome bucket list. Stop by a local coffee shop in Downtown Rome for a farewell breakfast treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Depending on departure time, do a final sweep of Downtown Rome for any last souvenirs or gallery visits. Head to the airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / travel day.

meals.dinner: Airport or travel food depending on departure schedule
